stories.title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
stories.simple_summary: A company called Cal AI made $30 million in two years through social media influencers promoting it, and then another company bought it.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and business people watching tech companies. If you are not buying or selling a business, there is nothing you need to do.

stories.title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
stories.simple_summary: ChatGPT's tool for Chrome (the web browser) can now look at the other tabs you have open when you ask it questions. You have to give it permission first.
stories.why_it_matters: This is useful if you want ChatGPT to help you research something across multiple web pages, but it also means being careful about what sensitive information you have open in other tabs.

stories.title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
stories.simple_summary: A video game company released an updated version of an old game that had so many problems it stopped selling it. One issue was that the game used AI to make pictures look better, but did it poorly.
stories.why_it_matters: If you buy video games, this shows that sometimes new versions of old games do not work well. You may want to wait for reviews before buying an updated game.

stories.title: Senate poised to add Claude to staffers’ AI tools
stories.simple_summary: The Senate is planning to let staff members use Claude, an AI assistant similar to ChatGPT, to help with their work.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that AI tools are becoming common in regular jobs even in government. There is nothing you need to do unless you work there.

stories.title: The tech backlash is now in theaters
stories.simple_summary: Several movies coming out in 2026 are being made about big tech company leaders, and they show these leaders in a negative way instead of celebrating them.
stories.why_it_matters: This reflects that more people are questioning whether some tech companies are good for society. This does not affect you directly, but it shows changing attitudes.

stories.title: Amazon introduces 2 new AI products from Bee: Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse
stories.simple_summary: Amazon announced two new AI products with names like Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse, but the details are not clear from this headline.
stories.why_it_matters: Without more information about what these products do, it is hard to say if they matter to you. Keep watching to learn what Amazon is offering.

stories.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
stories.simple_summary: President Trump posted pictures of White House repairs on social media, but at least one picture appears to have been edited with AI to make the work look better than it actually is.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a reminder that AI can change photos in ways that are hard to spot. Be cautious about believing what you see in pictures on social media.

stories.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
stories.simple_summary: Meta and Apple made an AI tool together that can run directly on your Mac computer without sending information to the internet.
stories.why_it_matters: This means some AI work could stay private on your own computer. This is mostly important for people who care about privacy or use newer Macs.

stories.title: Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social
stories.simple_summary: A social media site called Bluesky now has a tool that lets anyone create simple games, polls, and other small programs to share with others, using AI to help build them.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Bluesky and want to create interactive things to share, this tool makes it easier. Most people can ignore this unless they use that specific social media site.

stories.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps
stories.simple_summary: Amazon says in the future, AI devices in your home might predict what you want and do things for you without you having to ask them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly speculation about the future. Right now, you still have to ask Alexa and other smart devices to do things for you.

stories.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, a company that makes AI, gave researchers permission to study their AI and publish whatever they find, including problems and risks, without letting Anthropic block the results.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people watching AI companies. It shows one company is willing to be transparent about its AI systems.

stories.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more
stories.simple_summary: Bluesky is letting people on its social network build interactive websites and games using AI help, making coding easier even if you have never done it before.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Bluesky, this tool makes it simpler to create things to share. If you use other social media, this does not affect you right now.
